meta.description: Infer gene regulatory networks (GRNs) from gene expression data using scalable algorithms (GRNBoost2, GENIE3). Use when analyzing transcriptomics data (bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq) to identify transcription factor-target gene relationships and regulatory interactions. Supports distributed computation for large-scale datasets.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabrication; accurately describes established GRN inference algorithms (GRNBoost2, GENIE3) from peer-reviewed methods

practice_boundaries.detail: Appropriate scope for computational GRN inference; does not overstate biological causality from correlation-based methods

methodological_ground.detail: Based on validated tree-based ensemble regression methods published by Aerts Lab; reproducibility guidance with seed setting included

code_usability.detail: All code examples are executable with proper imports and multiprocessing guards; includes working script in scripts/ directory

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive coverage of GRN inference workflows, algorithm selection, distributed computing, and integration with pySCENIC; minor: lacks explicit statistical significance testing guidance

reliability.note: Good error handling in troubleshooting section covering memory errors, slow performance, Dask issues, empty results, and sparse data; reproducibility guidance strong with seed setting; minor: no explicit retry or failure recovery patterns

performance_context.note: Well-organized documentation (268 lines), clear sections with progressive disclosure through reference files; could benefit from performance benchmarks or timing estimates

agent_usability.note: Clear trigger description with specific use cases (transcriptomics, TF-target relationships); good examples; implicit 'When to Use' through description; minor: no explicit 'When NOT to Use' section

human_usability.note: Excellent setup with installation options (pip, conda), critical multiprocessing guard warning prominently placed, ready-to-run script provided, troubleshooting section actionable

security.note: No security concerns; computational tool with no credential management, network access, or user input risks; proper data format validation implied

maintainability.note: Good structure with version 1.0, license (BSD-3-Clause), reference files, scripts directory; notes upstream version (PyPI 0.1.6); missing: changelog or known issues section

agent_specific.note: Strong composability with pySCENIC integration and AnnData conversion; clear output format (TF, target, importance); reproducibility via seed parameter; minor: no explicit idempotency discussion, output format lacks schema validation

key_strengths: Critical multiprocessing guard (if __name__ == '__main__':) prominently documented with rationale, preventing common Dask spawn errors
Excellent algorithm comparison guidance (GRNBoost2 vs GENIE3) with clear default recommendation for most use cases
Strong reproducibility practices with seed parameter emphasized throughout examples and dedicated reproducibility section
Comprehensive distributed computing coverage from local multi-core to remote cluster with concrete Dask patterns
Clear integration pathway with pySCENIC ecosystem including AnnData conversion and downstream workflow context

recommendations.title: Add explicit 'When NOT to Use' section
recommendations.problem: Skill lacks boundary documentation for inappropriate use cases
recommendations.root_cause: Description focuses on positive triggers without exclusion criteria
recommendations.fix: Add 'When NOT to Use' section: Do not use for causal inference (use experimental perturbation data), small sample sizes (n<10 observations), or real-time analysis (computationally intensive)

recommendations.title: Quantify performance benefits of optimizations
recommendations.problem: TF filtering and distributed computing described but performance impact not quantified
recommendations.root_cause: Optimization techniques mentioned without scaling guidance
recommendations.fix: Add performance notes: e.g., 'TF filtering reduces runtime by 5-10x for typical datasets', 'distributed computing scales near-linearly up to ~20 workers for 10k+ observations'

recommendations.title: Statistical significance testing guidance missing
recommendations.problem: Consensus network aggregation shown but no statistical validation approach
recommendations.root_cause: Importance scores used directly without significance testing framework
recommendations.fix: Add section on statistical validation: permutation tests for null distribution, FDR correction for multiple testing, or reference to external tools like SCENIC's ctx pruning for regulatory evidence

recommendations.title: Add changelog or known issues section
recommendations.problem: Upstream version noted (0.1.6 from 2021) but no maintenance status or known issues documented
recommendations.root_cause: Maintainability affected by lack of version history and issue tracking
recommendations.fix: Add note about upstream maintenance status and link to GitHub issues; document any known limitations with newer Python versions or dependencies
